255.aliases: chapter 3 | candlestick basics | how to read candles

256.title: TradingView & Chart Tools
256.summary: What the common tools of a charting platform do: layouts, timeframes, drawings, measurement, indicator settings, alerts and watchlists, and what none of them can do.
256.aliases: chapter 7 | charting tools | chart platform basics | tradingview basics

257.title: Putting It Together
257.summary: How structure, levels, candles, indicators, volume and risk fit together as layers of context, why uncertainty remains, and why having no position is a valid outcome.
257.aliases: chapter 10 | combining analysis | top-down analysis | putting it all together

258.title: Bearish Engulfing
258.summary: A bearish engulfing pattern is two candles after an advance: a bullish candle followed by a bearish candle whose body covers the whole of the first body.
258.aliases: bearish engulfing pattern | bearish engulfing candle

259.title: Bearish Harami
259.summary: A bearish harami is two candles after an advance: a long bullish candle, then a small candle whose body sits inside the first body. It shows buying pressure pausing.
259.aliases: bearish harami pattern | harami | bearish harami cross

260.title: Bullish Engulfing
260.summary: A bullish engulfing pattern is two candles after a decline: a bearish candle followed by a bullish candle whose body covers the whole of the first body.
260.aliases: bullish engulfing pattern | bullish engulfing candle | engulfing pattern

261.title: Bullish Harami
261.summary: A bullish harami is two candles after a decline: a long bearish candle, then a small candle whose body sits inside the first body. It shows selling pressure pausing.
261.aliases: bullish harami pattern | harami | harami cross

262.title: Candlestick Context & Confirmation
262.summary: A candle pattern's shape matters less than where it forms, what came before it, the timeframe, the volume and how the next candle closes.
262.aliases: candlestick confirmation | candlestick context | confirmation candle

263.title: Dark Cloud Cover
263.summary: Dark cloud cover is two candles after an advance: a bullish candle, then a bearish candle that opens higher and closes below the midpoint of the first body without covering it.
263.aliases: dark cloud cover pattern | dark cloud | dark-cloud cover

264.title: Doji
264.summary: A Doji is a candle whose open and close are almost the same price. It shows that neither buyers nor sellers won the period.

265.title: Dragonfly Doji
265.summary: A Dragonfly Doji opens and closes at or near its high and has a long lower wick. Sellers pushed price down and buyers recovered all of it.

266.title: Evening Star
266.summary: An evening star is three candles after an advance: a long bullish candle, a small-bodied candle, then a long bearish candle that closes well into the first body.
266.aliases: evening star pattern | evening doji star | bearish abandoned baby

267.title: Gravestone Doji
267.summary: A Gravestone Doji opens and closes at or near its low and has a long upper wick. Buyers pushed price up and sellers took all of it back.

268.title: Hammer
268.summary: A hammer is a candle with a small body at the top of its range and a long lower wick, forming after a decline. It shows that lower prices were rejected.
268.aliases: hammer candle | bullish hammer | pin bar

269.title: Hanging Man
269.summary: A hanging man is a hammer-shaped candle, a small body on top of a long lower wick, that forms after an advance. It is read as a caution, not a conclusion.

270.title: Inverted Hammer
270.summary: An inverted hammer is a candle with a small body at the bottom of its range and a long upper wick, forming after a decline. It depends heavily on confirmation.

271.title: Morning Star
271.summary: A morning star is three candles after a decline: a long bearish candle, a small-bodied candle, then a long bullish candle that closes well into the first body.
271.aliases: morning star pattern | morning doji star | abandoned baby | bullish abandoned baby

272.title: Piercing Line
272.summary: A piercing line is two candles after a decline: a bearish candle, then a bullish candle that opens lower and closes above the midpoint of the first body without covering it.
272.aliases: piercing pattern | piercing line pattern | piercing candle

273.title: Rising & Falling Three Methods
273.summary: Rising three methods is a long bullish candle, several small candles inside its range, then another long bullish candle closing higher. Falling three methods is the mirror: a pause inside a trend.
273.aliases: rising three methods | falling three methods | three methods

274.title: Shooting Star
274.summary: A shooting star is a candle with a small body at the bottom of its range and a long upper wick, forming after an advance. It shows that higher prices were rejected.
274.aliases: shooting star candle | bearish pin bar

275.title: Spinning Top
275.summary: A spinning top is a candle with a small body and wicks on both sides. Price moved in both directions and finished only slightly away from where it started.
275.aliases: spinning top candle | spinning tops | high-wave candle

276.title: Three Inside Up & Down
276.summary: Three inside up is a bullish harami followed by a third candle that closes higher. Three inside down is a bearish harami followed by a lower close. Each is a harami plus one candle of follow-through.
276.aliases: three inside up | three inside down | confirmed harami

277.title: Three Outside Up & Down
277.summary: Three outside up is a bullish engulfing pattern followed by a third candle that closes higher. Three outside down is a bearish engulfing followed by a lower close.
277.aliases: three outside up | three outside down | confirmed engulfing

278.title: Tweezer Top & Bottom
278.summary: A tweezer top is two neighbouring candles with matching highs after an advance. A tweezer bottom is two with matching lows after a decline. Each shows a price tested twice and not passed.
278.aliases: tweezer top | tweezer bottom | tweezers | tweezer pattern

279.title: Wicks & Rejection
279.summary: A wick shows prices that traded during a period but did not hold until the close. A long wick is often described as the market rejecting those prices.
279.aliases: candle wicks | shadows | tails | price rejection | rejection wick

280.title: Chart Types: Line, Bar, Candle & More
280.summary: Chart types are different ways of drawing the same price data. Line, bar, candlestick, Heikin Ashi, area and Renko charts each keep some information and leave some out.
280.aliases: chart types | line chart | bar chart | ohlc chart | heikin ashi | renko | area chart | candlestick chart

281.title: Channels
281.summary: A channel is a trend contained between two roughly parallel lines: a trend line on one side and a parallel channel line on the other. It describes the rhythm of a trend, not its future.
281.aliases: price channel | trend channel | ascending channel | descending channel | parallel channel

282.title: Parabolic SAR
282.summary: Parabolic SAR is a trend-following indicator that plots trailing dots below or above price; the dots speed up as a move extends and switch sides when price reaches them.
282.aliases: PSAR | Parabolic Stop and Reverse | SAR | parabolic stop and reverse

283.title: Position Trading
283.summary: Position trading is a style in which positions are held for weeks to months or longer, with attention on the larger trend and little on day-to-day movement.
283.aliases: position trader | long-term trading | position trade

284.title: Pullback Trading
284.summary: Pullback trading is an approach that waits for a temporary move against an established trend, on the idea that the trend may resume. Its risk is a pullback that becomes a reversal.
284.aliases: pullback trader | pullback strategy | buying the dip | trading pullbacks | retracement trading

285.title: Trend Following
285.summary: Trend following is an approach that acts in the direction of an established trend and makes no attempt to predict tops or bottoms. It endures many small losses in sideways markets.
285.aliases: trend trading | trend follower | following the trend | trend following strategy

286.title: Breakout Trading
286.summary: Breakout trading is an approach built around price leaving a range, level or pattern, on the idea that a new move may follow. Its characteristic cost is the failed breakout.
286.aliases: breakout trader | breakout strategy | trading breakouts | range breakout

287.title: Drawing Trend Lines
287.summary: A trend line tool draws a straight line through two points chosen by the user. The tool is simple, and the judgment about which points to use is where the difficulty lies.
287.aliases: trend line tool | how to draw a trend line | trendline drawing | channel tool | parallel channel

288.title: Measuring Tools
288.summary: A measuring tool reports the distance between two points on a chart as a price change, a percentage change, a number of bars and an amount of time. It measures the past and nothing more.
288.aliases: measure tool | price range tool | date range tool | ruler tool | chart ruler | long position tool | risk reward tool

289.title: Price Scales: Log vs Linear
289.summary: A linear price scale gives equal space to equal price changes, while a logarithmic scale gives equal space to equal percentage changes. The same data can look very different on each.
289.aliases: log scale | logarithmic scale | linear scale | arithmetic scale | log chart | semi-log chart | price axis scale

290.title: Timeframes on a Chart
290.summary: A chart's timeframe sets how much time each candle covers. Changing it regroups the same trades into different candles, which changes the picture and every indicator value.
290.aliases: chart timeframe | candle interval | time interval | 1h chart | 4h chart | daily chart | switching timeframes

291.title: Watchlists & Layouts
291.summary: A watchlist is a saved list of market symbols, and a layout is a saved arrangement of a chart with its timeframe, indicators and drawings. Both organise attention and neither analyses anything.
291.aliases: watchlist | watch list | chart layout | saved layout | multi-chart layout | chart template | workspace

292.title: Choosing a Timeframe
292.summary: A chart timeframe sets how much time each candle covers. The timeframe a trader uses usually follows from the holding period, the time available and the weight of costs.
292.aliases: which timeframe | best timeframe | chart timeframe | trading timeframe | timeframe selection

293.title: Mean Reversion
293.summary: Mean reversion is an approach built on the idea that a price stretched far from its average may move back toward it. Its characteristic risk is a trend that does not revert.
293.aliases: mean reversion trading | reversion to the mean | mean-reversion strategy | fading | counter-trend trading

294.title: Overview of Trading Styles
294.summary: A trading style describes how long positions are usually held and what kind of price behaviour an approach is built around. No single style suits everyone.
294.aliases: trading styles | types of trading | types of traders | trading approaches

295.title: Swing Trading
295.summary: Swing trading is a style in which positions are held for days to weeks, with the aim of taking part in one swing of price inside a larger move.
295.aliases: swing trader | swing trade | swing trading strategy

296.title: Head and Shoulders
296.summary: A head and shoulders is three peaks after an advance, with the middle one highest, and a neckline under the two lows between them. It is conventionally read as a possible reversal if the neckline breaks.
296.aliases: head and shoulders top | H&S | head and shoulders pattern

297.title: Inverse Head and Shoulders
297.summary: An inverse head and shoulders is three lows after a decline, with the middle one deepest, and a neckline over the two highs between them. It is conventionally read as a possible reversal if the neckline breaks.
297.aliases: inverted head and shoulders | head and shoulders bottom | reverse head and shoulders | IH&S

298.title: Rounded Top & Rounded Bottom
298.summary: A rounded top or bottom is a slow, curved change of direction with no sharp turning point. It describes a trend that fades gradually, and it is usually clear only after it has finished.
298.aliases: rounding bottom | rounding top | saucer | saucer bottom | bowl pattern | dome

299.title: Triple Top & Triple Bottom
299.summary: A triple top is three peaks at a similar height; a triple bottom is three lows at a similar depth. Each is conventionally read as a possible reversal once the opposite side of the range breaks.
299.aliases: triple top | triple bottom | triple top pattern | triple bottom pattern

300.title: Combining Indicators
300.summary: Combining indicators means choosing tools that measure different things, because indicators from the same family are built from the same data and repeat the same information.
300.aliases: indicator confluence | multiple indicators | indicator redundancy | multicollinearity | indicator stacking

301.title: Rectangle
301.summary: A rectangle is a sideways pause in which price moves between two roughly horizontal boundaries. It describes balance between buyers and sellers and can resolve in either direction.
301.aliases: rectangle pattern | trading range | box pattern | consolidation range | congestion area

302.title: Bear Flag
302.summary: A bear flag is a sharp fall followed by a short, tight drift upward between two roughly parallel lines. It is conventionally read as a pause in a decline, and it often resolves the other way.
302.aliases: bearish flag | bear flag pattern | inverted flag

303.title: Bull Flag
303.summary: A bull flag is a sharp rise followed by a short, tight drift downward between two roughly parallel lines. It is conventionally read as a pause in an advance, and it often fails.
303.aliases: bullish flag | flag pattern | bull flag pattern

304.title: Cup and Handle
304.summary: A cup and handle is a rounded dip and recovery to a prior high, followed by a smaller pullback. It is conventionally read as a pause within an advance, completed if price closes above the rim.
304.aliases: cup with handle | cup and handle pattern | cup & handle

305.title: Pennant
305.summary: A pennant is a sharp move followed by a brief pause in which highs fall and lows rise into a small triangle. It is conventionally read as a continuation pattern, in either direction.
305.aliases: pennant pattern | bull pennant | bear pennant | bullish pennant | bearish pennant

306.title: Symmetrical Triangle
306.summary: A symmetrical triangle is a series of lower highs and higher lows that converge toward a point. It shows a market in shrinking balance and has no built-in direction.
306.aliases: symmetrical triangle pattern | symmetric triangle | coil | contracting triangle

307.title: ADX (Average Directional Index)
307.summary: ADX measures how strong a trend has been on a scale from 0 to 100, without saying which way it points; its companion lines +DI and -DI describe direction.
307.aliases: ADX | Average Directional Index | DMI | Directional Movement Index | +DI | -DI

326.title: ATH
326.summary: The highest price an asset has ever traded at, short for all-time high.

327.title: ATL
327.summary: The lowest price an asset has ever traded at, short for all-time low.

328.title: Ask
328.summary: The lowest price at which a seller is currently willing to sell, also called the offer.

329.title: Bid
329.summary: The highest price at which a buyer is currently willing to buy.

330.title: Spread
330.summary: The difference between two prices, most often the gap between the best bid and the best ask.

331.title: Order Book
331.summary: The live list of all open buy and sell orders for a market, arranged by price.

332.title: Market Order
332.summary: An order to buy or sell immediately at the best prices currently available.

333.title: Limit Order
333.summary: An order to buy or sell at a specified price or better, which waits in the order book until it can be filled.

334.title: Stop Order
334.summary: An order that stays inactive until price reaches a chosen trigger level, then becomes a market or limit order.
334.aliases: stop orders | stop-market order | stop-limit order

335.title: Stop Loss
335.summary: An order placed in advance to close a position if price moves against it to a chosen level, limiting the planned loss.

336.title: Take Profit
336.summary: An order placed in advance to close a position at a chosen price in the profitable direction.

337.title: Slippage
337.summary: The difference between the price expected when an order is sent and the price at which it actually fills.

338.title: Liquidity
338.summary: How easily an asset can be bought or sold in size without moving its price much.

339.title: Volume
339.summary: The total amount of an asset traded during a given period.

340.title: Volatility
340.summary: How much and how quickly a price moves up and down over a period.

341.title: Long
341.summary: A position that gains value when the price rises and loses value when it falls.

342.title: Short
342.summary: A position that gains value when the price falls and loses value when it rises.
342.aliases: short position | going short | short selling

343.title: Position
343.summary: The amount of an asset or contract a trader currently holds, either long or short.

344.title: Entry
344.summary: The price and moment at which a position is opened.

345.title: Exit
345.summary: The price and moment at which a position is closed, whether at a profit or at a loss.

346.title: PnL
346.summary: Profit and loss: the money gained or lost on a position or over a period.

347.title: Realized PnL
347.summary: The profit or loss that has been locked in by closing a position or part of it.
347.aliases: realized P&L | realised PnL | realized profit and loss

348.title: Unrealized PnL
348.summary: The profit or loss on a position that is still open, based on the current price.
348.aliases: unrealized P&L | unrealised PnL | floating PnL | paper profit

349.title: Leverage
349.summary: Using borrowed funds or margin to control a position larger than your own capital, which multiplies both gains and losses.

350.title: Margin
350.summary: The funds a trader sets aside as security to open and keep a leveraged position.

351.title: Initial Margin
351.summary: The minimum amount of collateral required to open a leveraged position.

352.title: Maintenance Margin
352.summary: The minimum collateral that must remain in a leveraged position to keep it open.

353.title: Collateral
353.summary: Assets pledged as security for a loan or a leveraged position.

354.title: Isolated Margin
354.summary: A margin mode in which each position has its own separate margin, so its liquidation normally consumes only that amount.

355.title: Cross Margin
355.summary: A margin mode in which the whole account balance is shared as margin across all open positions.

356.title: Liquidation
356.summary: The forced closing of a leveraged position by the exchange or protocol when its margin no longer covers its losses.

357.title: Liquidation Price
357.summary: The price at which a leveraged position's margin falls to the maintenance requirement and liquidation begins.

358.title: Margin Call
358.summary: A notice that an account's margin has fallen too low and that more funds must be added or positions reduced.

359.title: Maker
359.summary: A trader whose order rests in the order book and adds liquidity until someone else trades against it.

360.title: Taker
360.summary: A trader whose order fills immediately against orders already resting in the order book, removing liquidity.

361.title: Fill
361.summary: The execution of an order, in whole or in part.

362.title: Timeframe
362.summary: The length of time each candle or bar on a chart represents, such as one hour or one day.

363.title: OHLC
363.summary: The four prices that summarise a period of trading: open, high, low and close.

364.title: Candlestick
364.summary: A chart symbol that shows the open, high, low and close of one time period as a thick body with thin lines above and below.

365.title: Body
365.summary: The thick part of a candlestick, spanning the opening and closing prices of the period.

366.title: Wick
366.summary: The thin line above or below a candlestick's body, showing the highest or lowest price reached in the period.
366.aliases: shadow | tail | upper wick | lower wick

367.title: Bullish
367.summary: Describing rising prices, or a view, pattern or condition associated with rising prices.

368.title: Bearish
368.summary: Describing falling prices, or a view, pattern or condition associated with falling prices.

369.title: Bull Market
369.summary: A prolonged period in which prices in a market are generally rising.

370.title: Bear Market
370.summary: A prolonged period in which prices in a market are generally falling.

371.title: Trend
371.summary: The general direction in which a price is moving over a chosen period: up, down or sideways.

372.title: Uptrend
372.summary: A series of higher highs and higher lows, showing that price has been rising over the period viewed.

373.title: Downtrend
373.summary: A series of lower highs and lower lows, showing that price has been falling over the period viewed.

374.title: Range
374.summary: A period in which price moves sideways between a rough upper boundary and a rough lower boundary.

375.title: Swing High
375.summary: A peak on a chart: a high with lower highs on both sides of it.

376.title: Swing Low
376.summary: A trough on a chart: a low with higher lows on both sides of it.

377.title: Higher High
377.summary: A swing high that is above the previous swing high.

378.title: Higher Low
378.summary: A swing low that is above the previous swing low.

379.title: Lower High
379.summary: A swing high that is below the previous swing high.

380.title: Lower Low
380.summary: A swing low that is below the previous swing low.

381.title: Support
381.summary: A price area where buying has previously been strong enough to stop or slow a decline.

382.title: Resistance
382.summary: A price area where selling has previously been strong enough to stop or slow a rise.

383.title: Breakout
383.summary: A move in which price pushes above a resistance level or out of a chart pattern.

384.title: Breakdown
384.summary: A move in which price falls below a support level or out of the bottom of a chart pattern.

385.title: Fakeout
385.summary: A move beyond a support or resistance level that quickly reverses back inside the prior range.
385.aliases: false breakout | failed breakout | bull trap | bear trap

386.title: Retest
386.summary: A return of price to a level it has just broken, approaching it from the other side.

387.title: Pullback
387.summary: A temporary move against the prevailing trend, after which the trend may or may not resume.

388.title: Correction
388.summary: A decline that retraces part of a previous advance, usually larger or longer than a pullback.

389.title: Consolidation
389.summary: A pause in which price moves sideways in a relatively narrow area after a directional move.

390.title: Confluence
390.summary: The situation where several independent tools or observations point to the same price area or conclusion.

391.title: Trend Line
391.summary: A straight line drawn on a chart connecting successive swing lows in an uptrend or swing highs in a downtrend.

392.title: Channel
392.summary: Two roughly parallel trend lines that contain price between them as it trends or moves sideways.
392.aliases: price channel | trend channel | ascending channel | descending channel

393.title: Gap
393.summary: An empty space on a chart where a period opens at a price clearly different from the previous close, with no trading in between.
393.aliases: price gap | gap up | gap down

394.title: Momentum
394.summary: The speed and strength of a price move, often measured as the change in price over a set number of periods.

395.title: Mean Reversion
395.summary: The tendency of a price or indicator to move back toward an average after moving far away from it.

396.title: Divergence
396.summary: A disagreement between price and an indicator, for example price making a higher high while the indicator makes a lower high.

397.title: Overbought
397.summary: An indicator convention for a reading in the upper zone of an oscillator's scale, such as RSI above 70.

398.title: Oversold
398.summary: An indicator convention for a reading in the lower zone of an oscillator's scale, such as RSI below 30.

399.title: Risk/Reward Ratio
399.summary: A comparison of the amount a trade plans to risk with the amount it aims to gain.
399.aliases: risk-reward ratio | risk/reward | reward-to-risk ratio | R:R

400.title: Position Sizing
400.summary: Deciding how large a position to open, usually from the amount of money that would be lost if the stop loss is hit.

401.title: Drawdown
401.summary: The decline in an account or asset from a peak to a later low, usually given as a percentage.

402.title: Win Rate
402.summary: The percentage of trades that end in a profit.

403.title: Expectancy
403.summary: The average amount a trading method has gained or lost per trade, combining win rate with the average size of wins and losses.

404.title: Risk of Ruin
404.summary: The probability that a series of losses reduces an account to the point where trading can no longer continue.

405.title: Hedge
405.summary: A position opened to reduce the risk of another position by gaining when the first one loses.

406.title: Scalping
406.summary: A trading style that aims to capture very small price moves over seconds or minutes, many times a day.

407.title: Day Trading
407.summary: A trading style in which positions are opened and closed within the same day, with none held overnight.

408.title: Swing Trading
408.summary: A trading style that holds positions for several days to a few weeks to capture individual price swings.

409.title: Position Trading
409.summary: A trading style that holds positions for weeks, months or longer, following large trends.

410.title: Backtesting
410.summary: Testing a set of trading rules on historical price data to see how they would have performed.

411.title: Overfitting
411.summary: Tuning a trading method so closely to past data that it captures random noise and fails on new data.

412.title: Technical Analysis
412.summary: The study of price charts, volume and indicators to describe market behaviour and form views about possible future moves.

413.title: Fundamental Analysis
413.summary: The study of an asset's underlying economic value, using factors such as earnings, usage, supply and the wider economy.

414.title: Doji
414.summary: A candle whose open and close are almost the same price, often read as indecision.

415.title: Hammer
415.summary: A candle with a small body near the top of its range and a long lower wick, appearing after a decline.

416.title: Shooting Star
416.summary: A candle with a small body near the bottom of its range and a long upper wick, appearing after an advance.

417.title: Engulfing Pattern
417.summary: A two-candle pattern in which the second candle's body completely covers the body of the first, in the opposite direction.
417.aliases: engulfing | engulfing candle | bullish engulfing | bearish engulfing

418.title: Harami
418.summary: A two-candle pattern in which a small second body sits entirely inside the body of the larger candle before it.

419.title: Marubozu
419.summary: A candle with a long body and little or no wick at either end.

420.title: Spinning Top
420.summary: A candle with a small body and upper and lower wicks of similar, moderate length.

421.title: Morning Star
421.summary: A three-candle pattern after a decline: a long down candle, a small-bodied candle, then a long up candle.

422.title: Evening Star
422.summary: A three-candle pattern after an advance: a long up candle, a small-bodied candle, then a long down candle.

423.title: Double Top
423.summary: A chart pattern with two peaks at a similar level separated by a trough, forming a shape like the letter M.

424.title: Double Bottom
424.summary: A chart pattern with two troughs at a similar level separated by a peak, forming a shape like the letter W.

425.title: Head and Shoulders
425.summary: A chart pattern of three peaks, with the middle peak (the head) higher than the two on either side (the shoulders).
425.aliases: head-and-shoulders | inverse head and shoulders | H&S

426.title: Triangle Pattern
426.summary: A chart pattern in which price swings narrow between two converging trend lines.
426.aliases: ascending triangle | descending triangle | symmetrical triangle

427.title: Wedge Pattern
427.summary: A chart pattern in which price narrows between two converging trend lines that both slope in the same direction.

428.title: Flag Pattern
428.summary: A chart pattern in which a sharp move is followed by a short, narrow channel that slopes against that move.

429.title: Pennant
429.summary: A chart pattern in which a sharp move is followed by a small symmetrical triangle of narrowing price swings.

430.title: Cup and Handle
430.summary: A chart pattern made of a rounded, U-shaped decline and recovery (the cup) followed by a smaller pullback (the handle).

431.title: Indicator
431.summary: A calculation based on price, volume or both, drawn on a chart to summarise some aspect of market behaviour.

432.title: Oscillator
432.summary: An indicator that moves back and forth within a fixed range or around a centre line, used mainly to gauge momentum.

433.title: Moving Average
433.summary: The average price over a set number of recent periods, recalculated with each new candle and drawn as a line on the chart.

434.title: SMA
434.summary: The plain average of closing prices over a set number of periods, with every period weighted equally.

435.title: EMA
435.summary: A moving average that gives more weight to recent prices, so it reacts faster than a simple moving average.

436.title: RSI
436.summary: A momentum indicator on a 0-100 scale that compares recent gains with recent losses.

437.title: MACD
437.summary: A momentum indicator built from the difference between two exponential moving averages of price, usually 12 and 26 periods.

438.title: Signal Line
438.summary: A moving average of an indicator's own values, plotted alongside it to make its turns easier to see.

439.title: Histogram
439.summary: A display of values as bars; on the MACD it shows the distance between the MACD line and its signal line.

440.title: Stochastic Oscillator
440.summary: A momentum indicator on a 0-100 scale that shows where the latest close sits within the high-low range of recent periods.

441.title: Bollinger Bands
441.summary: A volatility indicator made of a moving average with one band above and one below it, set a number of standard deviations away.

442.title: ATR
442.summary: A volatility indicator that averages the true range of recent periods, showing how much price typically moves per candle.

443.title: VWAP
443.summary: The average price traded during a session, with each trade weighted by its volume.
443.aliases: Volume-Weighted Average Price | volume weighted average price

444.title: OBV
444.summary: A cumulative volume indicator that adds a period's volume when price closes higher and subtracts it when price closes lower.

445.title: ADX
445.summary: An indicator on a 0-100 scale that measures how strong a trend is, without showing its direction.

446.title: Volume Profile
446.summary: A chart tool that shows how much volume traded at each price level over a chosen period, drawn as horizontal bars.

447.title: Point of Control
447.summary: The price level with the highest traded volume in a volume profile.

448.title: Golden Cross
448.summary: A moving average crossover in which a shorter average, typically the 50-period, rises above a longer one, typically the 200-period.

449.title: Death Cross
449.summary: A moving average crossover in which a shorter average, typically the 50-period, falls below a longer one, typically the 200-period.

450.title: Market
450.summary: Any place or system where buyers and sellers meet to exchange assets and where prices are formed.

451.title: Asset
451.summary: Anything of value that can be owned and traded, such as a stock, bond, commodity, currency or cryptocurrency.

452.title: Stock
452.summary: A unit of ownership in a company, also called a share or equity.

453.title: Bond
453.summary: A loan made by an investor to a government or company, which pays interest and returns the principal at a set date.

454.title: ETF
454.summary: A fund that holds a basket of assets and whose shares trade on a stock exchange like an ordinary stock.

455.title: Index
455.summary: A calculated number that tracks the combined price of a defined group of assets, such as the largest companies in a country.

456.title: Commodity
456.summary: A basic physical good that is interchangeable with other units of the same kind, such as gold, oil or wheat.

457.title: Forex
457.summary: The global market in which national currencies are exchanged for one another.

458.title: Derivative
458.summary: A contract whose value is based on the price of something else, called the underlying asset.

459.title: Futures Contract
459.summary: A standardised agreement to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a set future date.

460.title: Perpetual Futures
460.summary: A futures contract with no expiry date, kept close to the spot price by regular funding payments between longs and shorts.
460.aliases: perpetual future | perpetual contract | perpetual swap | perpetuals | perps

461.title: Option
461.summary: A contract that gives its buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price up to or on a set date.
461.aliases: options | options contract | premium | strike price | expiry

462.title: Call Option
462.summary: An option that gives its buyer the right to buy the underlying asset at the strike price.

463.title: Put Option
463.summary: An option that gives its buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at the strike price.

464.title: Spot
464.summary: The market in which assets are bought and sold for immediate delivery at the current price.
464.aliases: spot market | spot trading | spot price

465.title: Exchange
465.summary: A marketplace, physical or electronic, where buyers and sellers trade assets under a common set of rules.

466.title: Broker
466.summary: A firm or person that places trades in a market on behalf of clients.

467.title: Market Maker
467.summary: A firm or trader that continuously quotes both a buy price and a sell price, providing liquidity to other participants.

468.title: Arbitrage
468.summary: Buying an asset in one market and selling it in another at nearly the same time to capture a difference in price.

469.title: Market Cap
469.summary: The total market value of an asset, calculated as its current price multiplied by its circulating supply.

470.title: Inflation
470.summary: A general rise in the prices of goods and services over time, which reduces what each unit of money can buy.

471.title: Interest Rate
471.summary: The cost of borrowing money, or the reward for lending it, expressed as a percentage of the amount per year.

472.title: Bid-Ask Spread
472.summary: The difference between the highest price a buyer is offering (the bid) and the lowest price a seller is asking (the ask).

473.title: Retail Trader
473.summary: An individual who trades with personal money, as opposed to a professional trading on behalf of an institution.
473.aliases: retail traders | retail investor | retail investors

474.title: Institutional Trader
474.summary: A professional organisation that trades large sums, such as a fund, bank, pension scheme or trading firm.
474.aliases: institutional traders | institutional investor | institutional investors

475.title: Whale
475.summary: Informal term for a person or entity holding enough of an asset that their trades can noticeably move its price.

476.title: Capitulation
476.summary: A phase of intense selling in which many holders give up and sell at a loss, usually on high volume after a long decline.

477.title: Euphoria
477.summary: A phase of extreme optimism in which prices rise quickly and risks are widely ignored.

478.title: Funding Rate
478.summary: A periodic payment exchanged between long and short holders of a perpetual futures contract to keep its price near the spot price.
478.aliases: funding rates | funding fee | funding payment

479.title: Open Interest
479.summary: The total number of derivative contracts that are currently open and have not been closed or settled.

480.title: Mark Price
480.summary: A reference price calculated by a derivatives exchange and used to value open positions and decide liquidations.

481.title: Index Price
481.summary: A reference price for an asset, calculated as an average of its spot price across several exchanges.

482.title: Basis
482.summary: The difference between the price of a futures contract and the spot price of the same asset.

483.title: Contango
483.summary: A market condition in which futures prices are higher than the spot price, and later expiries are priced above nearer ones.

484.title: Backwardation
484.summary: A market condition in which futures prices are lower than the spot price, and later expiries are priced below nearer ones.

485.title: Long/Short Ratio
485.summary: A statistic comparing the number of accounts, or the size of positions, that are long with those that are short on a derivatives exchange.
485.aliases: long-short ratio | long/short ratios | L/S ratio

486.title: Liquidation Cascade
486.summary: A chain reaction in which forced closures of leveraged positions push the price further, triggering more liquidations.

487.title: Short Squeeze
487.summary: A rapid price rise that forces holders of short positions to buy back, which adds to the buying and pushes the price higher still.

488.title: Auto-Deleveraging
488.summary: A last-resort mechanism in which a derivatives exchange closes part of profitable traders' positions to cover liquidation losses it cannot otherwise absorb.

489.title: Insurance Fund
489.summary: A pool of money held by a derivatives exchange to cover losses when a liquidated position loses more than the margin behind it.

490.title: Cryptocurrency
490.summary: A digital asset whose ownership and transfers are recorded on a blockchain and secured by cryptography instead of by a central institution.

491.title: Bitcoin
491.summary: The first cryptocurrency, a decentralized digital money whose supply is limited to about 21 million coins.

492.title: Satoshi
492.summary: The smallest unit of bitcoin: one hundred millionth of a bitcoin (0.00000001 BTC).

493.title: Ethereum
493.summary: A public blockchain that runs smart contracts, allowing programs and tokens to operate on a shared network.

494.title: Ether
494.summary: The native currency of the Ethereum network, used to pay transaction fees and staked by validators.

496.title: Coin
496.summary: A cryptocurrency that is the native asset of its own blockchain, such as bitcoin on Bitcoin or ether on Ethereum.

497.title: Token
497.summary: A crypto asset created by a smart contract on an existing blockchain, instead of being that blockchain's native coin.

498.title: Stablecoin
498.summary: A crypto token designed to hold a steady value, usually one US dollar.

499.title: Meme Coin
499.summary: A cryptocurrency based on an internet joke, image or cultural trend, with little or no intended function beyond that.

500.title: Blockchain
500.summary: A shared record of transactions grouped into blocks, where each block is cryptographically linked to the one before it.

501.title: Block
501.summary: A batch of transactions added to a blockchain as a single unit, together with a reference to the previous block.

502.title: Hash
502.summary: A fixed-length string of characters produced by running data through a mathematical function, acting as a digital fingerprint of that data.

503.title: Node
503.summary: A computer that runs a blockchain's software, keeps a copy of its data and passes transactions and blocks to other nodes.

504.title: Miner
504.summary: A participant in a proof-of-work network that uses computing power to compete for the right to add the next block.

505.title: Validator
505.summary: A participant in a proof-of-stake network that locks up coins as stake in order to propose and confirm new blocks.

506.title: Consensus
506.summary: The process by which the computers in a blockchain network agree on which transactions are valid and in what order.

507.title: Proof of Work
507.summary: A consensus method in which miners compete to solve a computational puzzle, and the winner adds the next block.

508.title: Proof of Stake
508.summary: A consensus method in which validators lock up coins as stake and are chosen to propose and confirm blocks.

509.title: Mining
509.summary: The process of using computing power to add new blocks to a proof-of-work blockchain in return for newly issued coins and transaction fees.
509.aliases: crypto mining | bitcoin mining | mining difficulty

510.title: Staking
510.summary: Locking up coins in a proof-of-stake network to help validate transactions, in return for rewards.

511.title: Slashing
511.summary: A penalty in proof-of-stake networks that destroys part of a validator's staked coins for provable misbehaviour.

512.title: Halving
512.summary: A scheduled event that cuts in half the number of new bitcoins created with each block.

513.title: Block Reward
513.summary: The payment a miner or validator receives for adding a block, made up of newly created coins plus transaction fees.

514.title: Mempool
514.summary: The waiting area where valid transactions sit after being broadcast and before being included in a block.

515.title: Confirmation
515.summary: The inclusion of a transaction in a block; each later block added on top counts as one more confirmation.

516.title: Finality
516.summary: The point at which a blockchain transaction can no longer be reversed or altered.

517.title: UTXO
517.summary: An unspent transaction output: a discrete chunk of bitcoin received in a past transaction that can be spent in a new one.

518.title: Gas
518.summary: The unit that measures how much computational work a transaction requires on Ethereum and similar blockchains.

519.title: Gas Fee
519.summary: The fee paid to a blockchain network to process a transaction, normally charged in the network's native coin.
519.aliases: gas fees | network fee | network fees | transaction fee

520.title: Smart Contract
520.summary: A program stored on a blockchain that runs automatically, exactly as written, when it is called by a transaction.

521.title: Layer 1
521.summary: A base blockchain that processes and finalises transactions on its own network, such as Bitcoin or Ethereum.

522.title: Layer 2
522.summary: A network built on top of a base blockchain that processes transactions off the main chain while relying on it for security.

523.title: Rollup
523.summary: A type of layer 2 that executes transactions off the main chain and posts compressed data or proofs back to it in batches.
523.aliases: rollups | optimistic rollup | ZK rollup | zk-rollup

524.title: Bridge
524.summary: A system that moves assets or data between two separate blockchains.

525.title: Fork
525.summary: A change to a blockchain's rules, or a split of one chain into two that share the same history up to that point.

526.title: Circulating Supply
526.summary: The number of coins or tokens that are currently available to the public and able to trade.

527.title: Total Supply
527.summary: The number of coins or tokens that exist right now, including locked or reserved ones, minus any that have been burned.

528.title: Max Supply
528.summary: The largest number of coins or tokens that can ever exist under an asset's rules.

529.title: FDV
529.summary: Fully diluted valuation: an asset's current price multiplied by its maximum supply.
529.aliases: fully diluted valuation | fully diluted market cap

530.title: Tokenomics
530.summary: The economic design of a crypto token: its supply, distribution, issuance schedule and uses.

531.title: Token Unlock
531.summary: A scheduled release of tokens that were previously locked, usually those allocated to a project's team, investors or treasury.
531.aliases: token unlocks | vesting schedule | cliff unlock

532.title: Emissions
532.summary: New tokens created and distributed over time as rewards, for example to miners, validators, stakers or liquidity providers.

533.title: Airdrop
533.summary: A distribution of tokens sent to many wallet addresses at no charge, usually to reward early users or publicise a project.

534.title: Governance Token
534.summary: A token that gives its holders the right to vote on decisions about a protocol, such as upgrades, fees or use of the treasury.

535.title: Utility Token
535.summary: A token intended to be used within a specific product or network, for example to pay fees or access a service.

536.title: Wallet
536.summary: Software or a device that stores the private keys used to control crypto assets and sign transactions.

537.title: Address
537.summary: A string of letters and numbers, derived from a public key, that identifies where crypto can be sent on a blockchain.

538.title: Public Key
538.summary: A cryptographic value derived from a private key that lets others verify signatures and from which addresses are generated.

539.title: Private Key
539.summary: A secret number that proves ownership of crypto at an address and is used to sign transactions that spend it.

540.title: Seed Phrase
540.summary: A list of usually 12 or 24 words that encodes the master secret from which all of a wallet's private keys are derived.
540.aliases: seed phrases | recovery phrase | secret recovery phrase | mnemonic phrase

541.title: Custodial
541.summary: Describing a wallet or service in which a third party, such as an exchange, holds the private keys on the user's behalf.

542.title: Non-Custodial
542.summary: Describing a wallet in which the user alone holds the private keys, with no custodian able to move or block the funds, although some tokens can still be frozen by their issuer.

543.title: Hot Wallet
543.summary: A crypto wallet whose private keys are kept on a device connected to the internet, such as a phone app or browser extension.

544.title: Cold Wallet
544.summary: A crypto wallet whose private keys are generated and kept offline, away from internet-connected devices.

545.title: Hardware Wallet
545.summary: A small dedicated device that stores private keys offline and signs transactions internally, so the keys never leave the device.

546.title: Signature
546.summary: Cryptographic proof, created with a private key, that the key's owner authorised a specific transaction or message.

547.title: Token Approval
547.summary: Permission given to a smart contract to move a set amount of a token from the user's wallet.
547.aliases: token approvals | token allowance | unlimited approval

548.title: CEX
548.summary: A centralized exchange: a company that runs a trading platform and holds customers' funds in its own custody.
548.aliases: centralized exchange | centralized exchanges | centralised exchange

549.title: DEX
549.summary: A decentralized exchange: a set of smart contracts that lets users trade tokens directly from their own wallets.
549.aliases: decentralized exchange | decentralized exchanges | decentralised exchange

550.title: DeFi
550.summary: Decentralized finance: financial services such as trading, lending and borrowing run by smart contracts on a blockchain instead of by companies.

551.title: AMM
551.summary: An automated market maker: a smart contract that prices trades with a mathematical formula applied to a pool of tokens, instead of matching orders.
551.aliases: automated market maker | automated market makers

552.title: Liquidity Pool
552.summary: A smart contract holding reserves of two or more tokens that traders swap against on a decentralized exchange.

553.title: Liquidity Provider
553.summary: Someone who deposits tokens into a liquidity pool so that others can trade against them, in return for a share of trading fees.

554.title: Swap
554.summary: An exchange of one crypto token for another, typically made directly against a liquidity pool on a decentralized exchange.

555.title: Price Impact
555.summary: The change in a market's or pool's price caused by a trade itself, which grows with the size of the trade relative to available liquidity.

556.title: Impermanent Loss
556.summary: The shortfall a liquidity provider has compared with simply holding the same tokens, caused by the pooled tokens' prices moving relative to each other.

557.title: TVL
557.summary: Total value locked: the combined market value of all assets deposited in a DeFi protocol or on a blockchain.

558.title: APR
558.summary: Annual percentage rate: a yearly rate of interest or reward that does not include the effect of compounding.

559.title: APY
559.summary: Annual percentage yield: a yearly rate of return that includes the effect of compounding.

560.title: Yield
560.summary: The income earned on an asset over time, such as interest, staking rewards or trading fees, expressed as a percentage of the amount held.

561.title: Lending
561.summary: Supplying assets to borrowers in return for interest; in DeFi this is done through smart contracts that pool deposits and lend against collateral.

562.title: Health Factor
562.summary: A number used by DeFi lending protocols to show how safely a loan is collateralized; below 1, the position can be liquidated.

563.title: KYC
563.summary: Know Your Customer: the identity checks that financial companies, including most centralized crypto exchanges, are required to carry out on their users.

564.title: Two-Factor Authentication
564.summary: A login method that requires a second proof of identity, such as a code from an app or a hardware key, in addition to a password.

565.title: Phishing
565.summary: A scam in which an attacker poses as a trusted company, site or person to trick someone into revealing secrets or approving a harmful action.

566.title: Wallet Drainer
566.summary: A malicious website or smart contract that tricks a user into signing a transaction or approval which hands over the assets in their wallet.

567.title: Rug Pull
567.summary: A scam in which a project's creators attract buyers and then take the funds, typically by withdrawing the liquidity or selling their holdings.

568.title: Honeypot
568.summary: A scam token whose smart contract lets people buy it but prevents them from selling.

569.title: Pump and Dump
569.summary: A scheme in which organisers buy an asset, promote it to drive the price up, then sell to the buyers they attracted.
569.aliases: pump-and-dump | pump and dump scheme | P&D

570.title: FOMO
570.summary: Fear of missing out: the anxiety of watching a price rise without being in the trade, and the urge to buy because others appear to be profiting.

571.title: FUD
571.summary: Fear, uncertainty and doubt: negative information or rumour, accurate or not, that spreads worry about an asset or project.

572.title: HODL
572.summary: Crypto slang for holding an asset for the long term regardless of price swings.

573.title: DYOR
573.summary: Do your own research: a reminder to check information independently before acting on someone else's claim.
